problem_statement: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery packets (Router Advertisement, Neighbor Solicitation, Neighbor Advertisement) received with an invalid IPv6 hop limit are not dropped on input. The input validation incorrectly treated a correct ICMPv6 code (0) as sufficient to accept the packet, so other field checks (such as the hop limit, multicast target, or source link-local requirement) were ignored whenever the code was valid. A malformed ND packet with a bad hop limit should be dropped and counted as a dropped ND packet, but instead it is silently passed through.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/ipv6 -s tests/net/ipv6/net.ipv6 -s net.ipv6 -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The problem statement clearly describes the bug (validation gated by ICMP code), the affected packet types (RA, NS, NA), and the expected behavior (bad hop limit → drop + count). The hidden tests use only pre-existing APIs (net_mgmt, NET_REQUEST_STATS_GET_IPV6_ND, struct net_stats_ipv6_nd with its drop field) and existing Kconfig options (CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS, CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS_USER_API) that a competent Zephyr developer would know about. No new names, behaviors, or exact values are required beyond what the statement provides.
